title: Entity-Anonymized Context Prompts for Improving Context Faithfulness in Knowledge-Conflict QA

contributions.purpose: Improve context faithfulness of LLMs in knowledge-conflict QA without training.
contributions.mechanism: Entity-Anonymized Context Prompts (EACP), a training-free method that replaces named-entity surface forms in context and question with anonymous placeholders (ENT_1, ENT_2) plus an entity inventory listing only types, then inverse-maps the placeholder answer back for evaluation.
contributions.evaluation: On ConFiQA-MC (6,000 examples, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), context-faithful rate Pc rises from 32.47% (control) to 74.75% (+42.28 points); memorization ratio drops from 37.82% to 12.59%.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that entity anonymization dramatically improves context faithfulness in knowledge-conflict QA, achieving a +42.28 point improvement in context-faithful answer rate on ConFiQA-MC.

contributions.purpose: Isolate anonymization as the causal active ingredient rather than the structured output format.
contributions.mechanism: Three-condition controlled experiment: A (O&I baseline), B (inventory+placeholder-ID output but real names), C (EACP with full anonymization); the critical C-vs-B comparison holds output format fixed.
contributions.evaluation: Condition B (Pc=32.47%) is worse than baseline A (Pc=52.43%) by -19.96 points; only C with anonymization succeeds, so format alone hurts and anonymization drives the gain.
contributions.source_quote: Through controlled experiments, we show that anonymization is the active ingredient--the structured output format alone actually hurts performance, and only anonymization produces gains.

contributions.purpose: Show EACP composes with activation steering and generalizes across model families.
contributions.mechanism: Combine EACP with ContextFocus activation steering, and replicate the A/B/C comparison on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in addition to Llama-3.1-8B.
contributions.evaluation: Combined EACP+ContextFocus reaches Pc=76.47% (vs 72.87% EACP-only, +3.60; vs 54.93% ContextFocus-only, +21.54) on 1,500 subset; Qwen shows +49.20 Pc gain (C vs B).
contributions.source_quote: We show that EACP is complementary to activation steering methods, with the combination achieving the best results, suggesting the two approaches address distinct failure modes.

contributions.purpose: Show a training-free prompting method can beat a training-based approach.
contributions.mechanism: Compare EACP against Context-DPO, a DPO fine-tuning method for context faithfulness.
contributions.evaluation: EACP achieves Pc=74.75% vs Context-DPO's reported 54.9%, without any fine-tuning (though on different base models).
contributions.source_quote: We show that EACP, a training-free prompting method, outperforms Context-DPO, a method requiring DPO fine-tuning, highlighting the effectiveness of simple prompt-level interventions.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Sheikhi et al. (2025) recently explored entity anonymization for improving knowledge attachment in dialogue generation, demonstrating that replacing entity names with placeholders can reduce hallucination. Our work extends this insight to knowledge-conflict question answering, providing controlled experiments that isolate the effect of anonymization from output format changes, and demonstrating complementarity with activation steering methods.
ContextFocus (Anand et al., 2026) steers model activations toward context-faithful representations using learned steering vectors.
Compared to Context-DPO (Bi et al., 2024), a training-based method requiring DPO fine-tuning, EACP achieves substantially higher context faithfulness (Pc=74.75% vs 54.9%) without any training.

notes: The Context-DPO comparison is acknowledged to be on different base models (Llama-3.1-8B vs Qwen2-7B), so it is not a clean head-to-head.
